beats.t: Up close, the tower looked taller still. Black water seeped between its bricks. Lightning at its summit neither struck nor vanished. It simply coiled there.
Sixteen, the Tower. Sudden collapse. Everything you've built, all at once.
Good card or bad card?
If you built it on lies, collapse is good. If you built something real, it hurts.
So both. Why are fortune-tellers always like this?
(A collapsing tower can be a good card. Then please, let only the lies collapse. Not us.)
Neo lifted himself from Yeoni's shoulder. His gaze hardened as he looked at the summit.
“Black Moon is up there. Head and tail. All together.”
Then we all go. You said no one should enter alone, remember? That includes you.
“I mustn't go in.”
That makes me want to bring you even more.
I'll take the front. That still stands, right?
Only half a step.
Inside the tower was nothing but stairs, spiraling upward along the outer wall. No railing. With every step, the drop below grew deeper.
Come up. I have prepared your place at the top.
The same voice echoed from every brick. Yeoni tightened the arm supporting Neo. Ahead, Seo Hanbi used her umbrella as a walking stick.
A step crumbled. Moka lost his footing. Yundal caught his tail with his gloved hand.
Don't grab my tail! It's part of my body!
Then give me your hand. And your birth date and time.
Now?!
While they bickered, bricks floated into the broken space one by one, reconnecting the stairs. Laughter lingered there briefly. Until it faded, the darkness below did not rise.
Two shadows followed along the wall. A head and a tail: Rahu and Ketu, who had hidden in the cards after the Vedic sky.
Those two are heading up. Faster than us.
Going to merge. Head and tail must meet to complete the eclipse.
Then run! We just have to get there first!
The stairs count our footsteps. Run, and they grow longer. This tower stretches for people in a hurry.
They walked with their breathing matched. Each time Neo exhaled, Yeoni climbed one step. Once everyone shared the same pace, the stairs stopped lengthening.
Rainwater. Why do you stand there, in front of that child? That is the face that took your envelope that spring.
I know now who borrowed that face.
Even knowing, does it not hurt to see it?
It hurts. That's why I stand in front. If the one who hurts takes the front, the person behind hurts less.
The voice in the wall paused. Yeoni looked at Seo Hanbi's back: wet coat, straight shoulders. Without a word, they touched her back once, then withdrew their hand.
The summit had no roof. A black sun hung in the center of the sky. Rahu and Ketu's shadows were drawn into it. Its rim flared red.
At last we meet face-to-face, vessel.
There was no face. Only red light circling the edge of round darkness. Yet Yeoni knew that darkness was smiling.
Stop saying vessel. I have a name. Yeoni.
A name. Yes, let us discuss names. The beast in your arms.
He occupies the last column of your Four Pillars. The Hour column. Gyeong. As long as he sits there, the vessel's lid stays closed.
[ Year: Im-o · Month: Byeong-o · Day: Eulhae · Hour: Gyeong-Chen ] 8/8
A lid? Then if Mr. Cat leaves, Yeoni...
Opens. And I enter. I have waited long.
Don't be ridiculous. I decide whom I put in my own Four Pillars.
Did you decide? He seated himself. Without your permission. Hiding even his name.
Yeoni's mouth closed. They couldn't deny it. He had hidden things: his wounds, his name, the first spring.
I'm angry he hid it. Very angry. But that's for me to confront him about. Not you.
Neo slipped his arm from Yeoni's shoulder. Their reaching hand passed through his sleeve. He stepped toward Black Moon.
Neo, come back. Don't stand in front of me.
“This time, I won't be late.”
Neo gathered the power remaining in his name. His transparent body became clear one final time. A long golden blade formed at his fingertips. The very power he had used to protect Yeoni.
That child is not a vessel. The place where I sit isn't a lid. It's a chair. One I brought so we could sit together.
Chair or lid. I need only remove it.
Neo, how long will that body last? Answer me.
Long enough for one scolding. Yeoni, wear matching socks.
That's your scolding now?! Don't talk like those are your last words!
Neo smiled. Strands of light scattered from the tips of his silver hair. They drifted toward Yeoni's feet and vanished before touching them.
Neo leaped toward the black sun. His golden blade split its red rim. With a sound like the sky tearing, lightning struck the tower's summit.
It's collapsing! The stairs!
Yeoni, this way! Grab the umbrella!
The floor tilted. Bricks rained down. The ground disappeared beneath Yeoni. Seo Hanbi held out the umbrella handle. Yeoni's fingers touched the tape, then slipped.
Yeoni fell through the collapsed floor. Neo kicked off the wall and caught them around the waist. Both their weights hung on one arm.
Grab my coat. Don't let go!
I can't! My hands go through!
Then I'll hold on.
Neo pushed Yeoni toward the remaining stairs. Yundal caught their wrist. Seo Hanbi held Yundal's waist; Moka held Seo Hanbi's coat.
Neo stayed below. Black hands seized his legs, waist, and cloak.
Neo! Neo!
Yeoni called only that name. No other. Two syllables of the three-syllable name rose to their lips; they clenched their teeth and swallowed them.
Well done. That's enough.
A nameless beast has little flavor. Still, Metal is Metal.
The black sun opened. Neo was dragged inside. Darkness covered the face that watched Yeoni until the very end. The sun closed.
Silence. Half the tower remained. The others lay tangled at the end of the broken stairs. The black sun was gone, withdrawn somewhere like a beast with a full belly.
[ Year: Im-o · Month: Byeong-o · Day: Eulhae · Hour: □-Chen ] 7/8
Yeoni stood and opened their palm. One golden thread lay across the scraped skin. They couldn't remember whose clothes it had come from.
(Where did this thread come from? Someone was wearing clothes with gold thread.)
Everyone okay? Is my tail intact? Wait, how many of us were there? Four?
Four. No, five. I think there was someone with a white umbrella.
Seo Hanbi stopped. White umbrella. Bus stop. The man who arrived late. His face was being rubbed out of her memory again.
No. He's someone we mustn't forget. I made him a promise. But what promise...
She pulled the ledger from her coat and flipped urgently through its palm-sized pages. Blank line, blank line, blank line. Rain had unraveled everything. Nothing remained.
Why now? Why is it all gone now? I should have written it down. Even one thing.
Don't cry. If you cry, I will too. I don't even know who it is. Why's my throat so tight?
Moka sniffled. Tears without a known reason. But the tears knew before the reason did: someone was missing.
There were five. Neo was here. A cat before, a person now... Someone who came with us.
Neo. I've heard that somewhere. Why can't I remember his face?
The name you gave him, Yeoni. You said it more than anyone.
How do you remember? It's all blurred for us.
Because I'm the one forgotten. I know what that feels like, so when someone else is forgotten, I hold on tight.
Yundal clenched and opened his gloved hand. The Void in his palm was very slightly warm. A thread of gold had caught inside it. He didn't mention it yet.
Yeoni's notebook fell from their bag and opened to the last page they had written. Their own handwriting, pressed hard.
[ Even in a different form, Neo. On my side. ]
This is my handwriting. I wrote it. But...
Yeoni traced the words with a finger. The paper was deeply indented, nearly torn by the force of writing. Something they had wanted that badly not to forget.
Why can't I remember? I pressed so hard. It says on my side. Who was on my side?
Yeoni. Trust those words. Memories can be erased, but your hand can't lie.
Who... was Neo?
